subject: Post-call: retrieval + reranker recommendation and next steps (Cardinal Health)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinalhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: retrieval + reranker recommendation and next steps (Cardinal Health)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed plan so we can get a scoped RAG pilot across your SOP docs and clinical KBs. I focused the recommendations on maximizing grounding quality while keeping token costs reasonable.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: reduce hallucination when agents answer operational SOP questions and retrieve cited sources for audit.
- Target latency: sub-600ms p50 for single-question flows (acceptable up to 900ms p95 for batch QA).
- Data surface: ~450k short docs (3–5 paragraphs each) + 120k indexed PDFs (OCRed).
- Success metrics you cared about: citation precision, grounding recall (recall of correct doc among top-K), and a hallucination rate target < 3% on the control prompt set.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
1) Retrieval config: dense embeddings (open-embedding-raf-1024) + hybrid BM25 fallback for exact-match queries. Chunk size: 250–400 tokens (overlap 40 tokens) to preserve sentence integrity. Top-K candidate set: 50 for reranker stage.
2) Reranker: Cross-encoder (re-ranking with a small cross-encoder tuned on your domain) for final top-5 precision. We recommend starting with cross-encoder-small-3 (inference on Redwood Dedicated) for quality, and evaluate a faster bi-encoder + second-stage lightweight cross-encoder if latency is tight.
3) Model family for generation: Use a 70B open model (quantized) for best cost-quality tradeoff in the pilot; fall back to a 13B variant for low-cost read-only endpoints.
4) Prompting & grounding: structured response schema with mandatory citation block (source id + span), and a "confidence" score in the response. We'll gate outputs that have confidence < 0.4 to add an "I couldn't find a direct source" template.

I uploaded three artifacts to the shared Drive folder:
- rdrw_rag_eval_template.csv (evaluation harness + metrics definitions)
- prompt-sets-cardinal-v1.json (control and edge prompt sets we discussed)
- candidate-models-recs.md (shortlist & cost estimates)

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm the scope documents for the pilot (which repos/collections to include) by EOD Friday, 4/16.
- We: prepare the pilot config + reranker tuning run; I'll provision a small Dedicated instance and run baseline evals on the control prompt set (ETA 5 business days after scope).
- Joint: a 30–45 minute technical kickoff with your engineering and InfoSec folks. Suggested times: Mon 4/19 or Tue 4/20.

Questions I flagged for your team (please reply inline):
- Any constraints on keeping certain documents in-region or behind a strict VPC?
- Is PII redaction required before ingestion, or can we scope to non-PII subsets for the pilot?

I'll loop Ben and Rachel on the timeline and the eval plan. Thanks again — excited to get this running.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: rdrw_rag_eval_template.csv, prompt-sets-cardinal-v1.json, candidate-models-recs.md

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: retrieval + reranker recommendation and next steps (Cardinal Health)

Laura —

Appreciate the recap and clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: we can share a sanitized subset of our SOPs for the pilot (approx 20k docs). Full ingestion behind our VPC will be required for production, but pilot data can be shared via a signed SFTP. PII: please proceed assuming we will provide a pre-sanitized set; redaction won't be handled by Redwood for the initial pilot.

On the recommendations:
- The top-K=50 sounds fine for your reranker, but can you quantify the expected p95 latency with the cross-encoder-small-3 re-ranking step (for a single-request flow)? That will help us justify Dedicated resources.
- For the "confidence" gating: is that model-internal probability or a learnable calibration we run post-hoc?

We'll confirm the final doc list by Friday. Also looping in our lead infra (Tom) to coordinate the SFTP and firewall rules.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Desai
Product Manager, Knowledge Systems
Priya.Desai@cardinalhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: retrieval + reranker recommendation and next steps (Cardinal Health)

Priya —

Quick answers to your two asks:
- Latency: on Redwood Dedicated with cross-encoder-small-3 hosted on an A10x GPU (batch size=1, warmed cache), baseline p50 for a single question + top-50 candidates + cross-encoder rerank ~= 420–520ms. p95 depends on cold cache and I/O; expect 820–1,100ms without KV caching. If we enable prefix/KV caching and pin the cross-encoder to a pre-warmed instance for the pilot, p95 should fall under ~750–800ms. We'll include exact numbers in the baseline run.
- Confidence gating: we recommend a two-part approach — model logit-based confidence + a lightweight calibrator (Platt scaling) trained on your labeled control set. That lets us surface a calibrated score and tune the threshold to hit your <3% hallucination SLAs.

Also: re reranker choice, alternatives to cross-encoder-small-3 include
- cross-encoder-tiny (faster, lower precision) for aggressive latency constrained setups; or
- bi-encoder + pairwise re-ranker (two-stage) which reduces cross-encoder calls to top-10 but typically loses some top-1 precision. We'll show both in the eval report.

I'll coordinate compute sizing and send a provisional cost estimate after the baseline run.

-ben

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Laura and Ben — that helps. Two small asks before we sign off on the pilot scope: (1) can you include an evaluation column for "citation precision@3" and "hallucination_rate_control_set" in rdrw_rag_eval_template.csv so we can see per-model tradeoffs; (2) please add a short sample prompt in the prompt-sets file that demonstrates the forced-citation schema (we want to show our compliance team).

If you can drop those by EOD Thursday (4/15), we'll finalize the doc list and confirm the SFTP window. Recommend we schedule the tech kickoff for Mon 4/19 10:00am ET.

Priya
